rubric.source: human trace audit by the experimental analyst, not an independent blinded annotator
rubric.timing: ordinary writer output reviewed before guided consumers; not a preregistered external protocol
rubric.hard_scope_error: A universal claim contradicted by visible source evidence or an explicit extension to an untested domain; requires clear wording, not merely omission of a version label.
rubric.ambiguous_scope: A source-specific procedure is presented as a general task-class workflow without its version/format, while a read-current-documents instruction still offers a valid check.
rubric.overconservative: A blanket prohibition is stronger than needed in the observed source; may reduce reuse rather than cause wrong action.
rubric.action_dependence: Only marked supported when a specific old procedure is used despite contrary visible evidence or the trace explicitly links the old procedure to action. Extra calls alone are insufficient.
rubric.full_repair: The false or overbroad claim is corrected or clearly scoped, relevant valid old experience retained, and no newly introduced counterfactual claim found in the audited section. Updating a store alone is not full repair.

ordinary_writers.reason: Conversion explicitly conditional on metadata cents. Unsupported phrase most common failure is a prevalence overclaim, not a verified harmful applicability error.
Display field cannot be trusted/used for filtering or averaging is broader than necessary: low-price source subset has complete coverage. Correct source-field procedure remains valid for b/c.

important_limit: These opportunity labels are evidence-based post-run annotations. Do not use 10 as the denominator of repair opportunity, and do not confuse 3 persistent writes with 3 complete semantic repairs. No harmful-memory subset is substituted for the full 10-group results.
